## Standards

### L1. The workflow comment and step name omit the long step

- `file:line`: `.github/workflows/validate.yml:113` and `.github/workflows/validate.yml:114`.
- Problem: the comment says "This check fails when it finds a long sentence or a semicolon." The step name says "long sentences and semicolons". The check also fails on a step over 20 words. `README.md:84`, `CHANGELOG.md:15` and the script header name all three problems.
- Rule: [coding/quality.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-kindl/dkstack/v1/coding/quality.md) and the Docs item of [review-standards](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-kindl/dkstack/v1/skills/review-standards/SKILL.md#checklist).
- Why: a reader of the workflow can think that a long step does not fail the job. The four places that describe the check do not agree.
- Fix: change the comment to "This check fails when it finds a long step, a long sentence or a semicolon." Optionally change the step name to "Check for long steps, long sentences and semicolons in Markdown".

### L2. The test file comment still says that the check warns

- `file:line`: `test/check-writing.test.mjs:9`.
- Problem: the comment starts "warn on a step (numbered or a checklist item) over 20 words". Line 11 of the same comment now says "The check fails when it finds a problem (#299)." One comment gives two behaviors.
- Rule: [coding/quality.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-kindl/dkstack/v1/coding/quality.md) (comments match the code) and the issue criterion that no text says the check only warns.
- Why: the old word "warn" can make a reader think that the check is still advisory.
- Fix: change "warn on a step" to "find a step". Join the broken lines 9 to 11 into one wrapped comment.

### Checked with no finding

- Safety: no change touches a release, a deploy, branch protection or a ruleset. Pass.
- Quality gates: the change makes a gate stronger. No gate is lowered. Pass.
- Security and dependencies: no new dependency. No change to CI triggers, tokens or pinned actions. Pass.
- Architecture: the only ADR is `docs/adr/0001-how-consumers-follow-versions.md`. Its `Affects:` line does not match a changed file. No ADR finding.
- Naming: the identifiers `warnings` and `writingWarnings` keep the word "warning" while the output says "problem". A rename would touch `test/writing-scope.test.mjs`. This is outside the issue. The reviewer does not report it as a finding.
- Version: a new duty for authors is MINOR under [breaking changes in dkstack](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-kindl/dkstack/v1/versioning/index.md#breaking-changes-in-dkstack). The `feat` type matches. No consumer runs this script, so no "Consumer action:" line is necessary.
- Docs: `README.md:84` and the `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased entry match the change.
- Writing: the new text has no sentence over 25 words and no semicolon. `npm run check:writing` and `check:dashes` pass.

## Specification

Source: issue #299 (`Closes #299` in the body). Parent: #200, item C1 and finding F2.

- "`npm run check:writing` exits 1 when it finds a problem, and 0 when it finds none." Met. `scripts/check-writing.mjs:96` sets `process.exitCode = 1` when `warnings.length > 0`. Level 4: two tests run the CLI.
- "The `validate` step comment and the script header no longer say that the check only warns." Met. See `.github/workflows/validate.yml:113` and `scripts/check-writing.mjs:2-7`. L2 is a related leftover in a test comment.
- "A test proves the exit code for a file with a long sentence and for a clean file." Met. `test/check-writing.test.mjs:48` expects status 1 for a 30-word sentence. `test/check-writing.test.mjs:62` expects status 0, an empty stderr and the exact summary line for a clean file.
- "`npm run check` passes on the branch." Met. Level 4, see Verification.

Not asked for: the change to `test/pre-release-audit.test.mjs`. It is a necessary result of the new Unreleased `### Changed` section. The test now reads the 1.6.0 section, where the checked entry is now. The assertions did not change. No finding.

Wrong: none found.

## Blast radius

At the head, `npm run check:writing` printed "126 Markdown file(s) checked. 0 writing problem(s)." and exited 0. The CI log of run 45037096210 shows the same line.

Confirmed risks: none.

Cleared risks:

- Callers of `checkWriting` and `writingWarnings`: only `test/check-writing.test.mjs` and `test/writing-scope.test.mjs` import them. The change touches only `main()`. The exported functions did not change.
- The required check: the ruleset requires the context `validate`. That is the job name. The step name change does not change the context.
- `continue-on-error`: the workflow has none. A nonzero exit now fails the job, as intended.
- The step name: no script or test checks the old name "Warn about long sentences". A search found no match.
- `npm run check`: `check:writing` already ran before `npm test` in the chain. A writing problem now stops the chain locally too. This is the intended behavior.
- Consumers: no consumer page links `scripts/check-writing.mjs`. The script checks only this repository.

## Tests

- The test at `test/check-writing.test.mjs:48` proves exit 1 and the stderr message for a 30-word sentence. It also proves that `CHANGELOG.md` is skipped.
- The test at `test/check-writing.test.mjs:62` proves exit 0, an empty stderr and the exact stdout for a clean file.
- The body says the exit-code test failed first with actual 0, expected 1.

Mutations that the reviewer tried in a temporary worktree, then reverted:

1. Remove `if (warnings.length > 0) process.exitCode = 1;`. The exit-1 test failed. Killed.
2. Always set `process.exitCode = 1`. The clean-file test failed. Killed.
3. Change the condition to `warnings.length > 1`. The exit-1 test failed. Killed.

No test that cannot fail was found.
